title: Git History and Best Practices
learning_objectives: Read and interpret git log output effectively
View file changes with git diff
Understand .gitignore and why certain files should never be committed
Write professional commit messages following best practices
Use git show to inspect specific commits
outline: Viewing changes: git diff (working vs staged vs committed)
The .gitignore file: Why and what to ignore
Commit message best practices: Structure, tone, length
Atomic commits: One logical change per commit
When to commit: Frequency and granularity guidelines
Hands-on exercise: Create comprehensive .gitignore for CatchBook

catchbook_context.deliverable: .gitignore file configured for React Native + Python backend

criteria: Can use git log with multiple flags to view history
Can use git diff to compare changes before committing
.gitignore file created with appropriate patterns (node_modules, __pycache__, .env, etc.)
Commits in CatchBook repo follow best practices (clear messages, atomic changes)
Can explain why certain files should be ignored
Demonstrates understanding of when to make a commit vs continue working

resources.title: Pro Git Book - Viewing the Commit History
How to Write a Git Commit Message

professor_constraints: Show real examples of good vs bad commit messages
Demonstrate git diff before staging to preview changes
Provide comprehensive .gitignore template for CatchBook tech stack
Explain why secrets (.env files) must never be committed
Use git log --graph --oneline --all to show visual history
Address 'oops, I committed sensitive data' scenario briefly (git rm --cached)
